rv.q: Adam Penford's capable revival lacks the comic elan that unlocks Ayckbourn's larger theme.
The director Lucy Bailey’s approach is to honor the savagery and poetry of the text in equal measure while also inflecting the show with humor.

cn.t: Ayckbourn's prescient satire on Thatcherism and moral compromise returns to the National, but critics find this capable revival lacks the comic sharpness needed to fully unlock the play's larger themes about greed and family values.
